dimensions.title: Cognitive
milestones: Recognizes familiar faces and objects
Begins to understand cause and effect
Explores objects by banging or shaking them
activities: Provide toys that make noise when shaken
Play peek-a-boo to enhance understanding of object permanence
Encourage problem-solving by presenting simple puzzles
watchFor: Lacks interest in toys or activities
Does not respond to familiar voices
Does not explore objects

dimensions.title: Language
milestones: Babbling or cooing frequently
Responds to own name
Begins to make sounds to express needs
activities: Read aloud daily
Sing simple songs and nursery rhymes
Encourage imitation of sounds
watchFor: Does not attempt to speak or produce sounds
Lack of response to verbal communication
Unusual sounds that do not resemble typical babbling

dimensions.title: Physical
milestones: Rolls over in both directions
Begins to sit without support
Reaches for and grasps objects
activities: Tummy time to strengthen neck and shoulder muscles
Offer toys that are easy to grasp
Encourage sitting by propping with pillows
watchFor: Does not roll over by 6 months
Weak arm or leg movements
Lack of progression in reaching and grasping

dimensions.title: Social
milestones: Smiles at people
Engages in social play with familiar caregivers
Shows a preference for certain people and toys
activities: Encourage playdates with other infants
Introduce games that involve turn-taking
Facilitate interactions with caregivers
watchFor: Does not smile at people
Shows no interest in social interactions
Frightened by new people or situations

dimensions.title: Emotional
milestones: Shows mood changes (happy, sad)
Begins to express frustration or displeasure
Self-soothes by sucking on hands or fingers
activities: Provide a secure and loving environment
Respond consistently to cries or needs
Introduce comfort items like a soft toy
watchFor: Excessive crying without a clear cause
Lack of emotional expression
Difficulty being comforted by caregivers

dimensions.title: Curiosity
milestones: Shows interest in surroundings
Explores objects using mouth and hands
Begins to anticipate outcomes of simple actions
activities: Create a safe exploration area with various textures
Introduce toys that encourage exploration like stacking toys
Encourage looking for hidden toys
watchFor: Disinterest in new experiences
Avoids exploring surroundings
Limited interaction with toys or objects

dimensions.title: Learning
milestones: Shows longer attention spans for activities
Recognizes familiar routines
Begins to anticipate what comes next in a sequence
activities: Establish daily routines and rituals
Introduce simple cause-effect toys
Play games that involve repetition
watchFor: Frequent distraction with inability to focus
Unfamiliarity with routine changes
Resistance to engaging in simple activities

dimensions.title: Independence
milestones: Attempts to feed self with fingers
Begins to show preferences for certain toys or foods
Responds to simple cues or requests
activities: Allow opportunities for self-feeding with safe finger foods
Encourage participation in simple choices (e.g., toy selections)
Provide toys that promote self-play
watchFor: Avoidance of self-feeding
Lack of interest in trying new things
Difficulty making choices or responding to simple cues
